facts.recipient: OpenAI-compatible LLM API set in application.chatBot.llmApiUrl (default localhost, config/default.yml:22)

verdicts.deciding: Passwords are stored as unsalted MD5, which is a fast digest and not a password hashing function.

Raw SQL is built by string interpolation from request data. MarsDB $where strings are built by concatenation. Request-body objects go straight into NoSQL selectors (operator injection). Sequelize ORM calls elsewhere are parameterized.
The session cookie 'token' is set with no Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite attribute and no __Host-/__Secure- prefix. Client-side JavaScript sets it in most places, so it cannot be HttpOnly.

routes/chat.ts trusts the user id and role from jws.decode without checking the signature. express-jwt 0.1.3 and jsonwebtoken 0.4.0 (package.json:109, package.json:123) are given no algorithm allowlist, so alg 'none' is accepted (the app's jwtUnsigned challenge relies on this, routes/verify.ts:125), and the RSA public key can be used as an HMAC secret.
The JWT RSA private key, the HMAC key, the cookie-signing secret, a wallet mnemonic, the CTF key and seeded user passwords and TOTP secrets are literals in source or in files loaded at run time.

The morgan 'combined' access log records full URLs and client IPs. Password change is a GET with current/new/repeat passwords in the query string (server.ts:636, routes/changePassword.ts:14), so passwords reach logs/access.log. errorhandler logs error stacks, which include SQL from routes/login.ts:34 with the email and password hash, and client IPs.

Passwords are the only factor for most accounts (TOTP is optional). The minimum is 5 characters and is checked only in the client; the server checks no length. That is below both 15 and 8. The client also caps passwords at 40 characters, below the recommended 64.
No composition rule is enforced. frontend/src/app/password-strength/password-strength.component.ts:31 is an advisory strength meter only.
New passwords set through registration, change or reset are not compared against any blocklist.
/rest/user/login has no rate limit or per-account lockout. The only limiter on reset-password is per IP, and the client controls its key through the X-Forwarded-For header.

An erasure request only writes a PrivacyRequests row (deletionRequested=true), and nothing reads it. DELETE /api/Users/:id is denyAll. User, address, card, basket and MarsDB order and review data are never erased.

Visitor IPs and OAuth data go to Google, a US company (frontend/src/index.html:15, frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:34, frontend/src/app/Services/user.service.ts:68). Usernames, chat text and order data go to whichever LLM endpoint the deployment configures (routes/chat.ts:108, routes/chat.ts:201). Whether a legal basis exists depends on things outside the repository: whether the operator relies on Google LLC's EU-US Data Privacy Framework certification or on SCCs/DPAs, and where the deployed LLM endpoint is hosted.

No cookie options are set, so express-session 1.15.6 defaults apply: HttpOnly is on, Secure is off, and SameSite is not set. The cookie name is connect.sid, with no __Host- or __Secure- prefix. The app serves plain HTTP (server.js:145).
No JWT or other self-contained token is used. Sessions are server-side through express-session.

The session signing secret and the crypto key are literals used in every environment. Seeded account passwords are written in the script that app.json:13 (postdeploy) and docker-compose.yml:9 run on deploy. The demo TLS key and the ZAP keys in dev/test config are marked as test/example.

1) At startup the full config is logged: cookieSecret, cryptoKey, and the db URI, which comes from MONGODB_URI and may embed credentials. 2) The deploy-time seed script logs user records with plaintext passwords. No session tokens are logged.
PASS_RE /^.{1,20}$/ allows a password of 1 character. The password is the only factor, so the minimum is 15. The maximum of 20 is also below the recommended 64 or more.
Only length is checked. The composition regex is commented out (session.js:148), although the error text at session.js:172 still claims rules apply.
Signup checks new passwords against no blocklist of common, expected, or compromised passwords.
POST /login has no attempt counter, lockout, throttling or rate-limit middleware.

The app stores names, email, SSN, DOB, address and bank details (profile-dao.js:42) but has no route or DAO method to delete an account or its data. An operator could still delete data directly in MongoDB outside the app.

pwdlib Argon2Hasher (argon2id, m=65536, t=3, p=4, random salt per hash, see the dummy hash at backend/app/crud.py:42) with bcrypt fallback, at backend/app/core/security.py:11. This meets ASVS Appendix C.
All queries use SQLModel/SQLAlchemy select/get/delete expressions with bound parameters. There is no raw SQL or text() and no string building. Path IDs are UUID-typed and skip/limit are int-typed.
No cookies are set. The JWT is returned in the response body and kept in localStorage (frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.ts:45, frontend/src/main.tsx:19), then sent as a Bearer header.

PyJWT jwt.decode checks the HMAC signature and exp against algorithms=['HS256'] (backend/app/core/security.py:19) before the payload is used (backend/app/api/deps.py:32, backend/app/utils.py:120). 'none' is not allowed.

The committed .env only holds 'changethis' placeholders (.env:6, .env:8, .env:17). backend/app/core/config.py:66-86 rejects these values unless FASTAPI_ENV=development. .env is not copied into the Docker image (backend/Dockerfile:48-52) and is excluded from FastAPI Cloud uploads (.fastapicloudignore:1). Real values come from env vars and CI secrets.

Traefik access logging is on, and it records the full request URI. The password-reset bearer token travels in the query string (backend/app/utils.py:73, GET /reset-password?token=...), and user emails travel in the path (backend/app/api/routes/login.py:53). So both are written to the access log with no masking. The application's own logger (backend/app/utils.py:57) logs only the SMTP status.
The password is the only login factor (no MFA anywhere), so the minimum must be 15 characters. The code enforces min_length=8. The maximum of 128 satisfies the 'at least 64' SHOULD.
Only length limits are enforced, in the backend models and the frontend zod schemas. There are no character-class rules.
New and changed passwords are hashed without any check against a common, expected or compromised password list.
There is no failed-attempt counter, lockout, delay or rate-limit middleware in the app or in the Traefik config.

Users can delete their own account (backend/app/api/routes/users.py:132-143) and admins can delete users (users.py:214-232). Items cascade (backend/app/models.py:55, 91). Superusers cannot delete themselves but can be deleted by another superuser. Copies in logs, backups or Sentry are operational matters outside the code.

Two transfers exist when configured: Sentry (backend/app/main.py:19) and the SMTP provider (backend/app/utils.py:56). Whether either goes outside the EEA, and on what basis, depends on the deployment. That means which SENTRY_DSN region or host is used (US sentry.io, EU region, or self-hosted), which SMTP_HOST provider is chosen and where it is located, and whether there is an adequacy decision, an EU-US DPF certification, or a DPA with SCCs. The repository cannot show any of this.

The pygoat raw files (code-raw-pygoat-1..3.txt) are not the original delivery captures. The original reply texts were lost when the orchestrator's context was compacted.
